reconcile.connective: Defenders read the two counts as one command refined: two of every kind for survival, with extra clean animals added for post-flood sacrifice — and deny this proves two spliced sources.

discrepancy.connective: Julius Wellhausen made the animal-count split a foundational case for the Documentary Hypothesis, assigning the seven clean pairs of Genesis 7:2 to the J source and the uniform two-of-each of Genesis 6:19 to the later Priestly writer, two flood accounts a redactor stitched together.

skeptic.name: Julius Wellhausen
skeptic.work: Prolegomena to the History of Israel
skeptic.attribution: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (ET 1885; German 1878/1883)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The fact that in the command to enter the ark a distinction is now made between clean and unclean animals, seven of the former being ordered to be taken, - i.e., three pair and a single one, probably a male for sacrifice-is no more a proof of different authorship, or of the fusion of two accounts, than the interchange of the names Jehovah and Elohim.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly engages and rebuts the source-critical reading of the two-vs-seven discrepancy (the exact objection Wellhausen presses): the seven clean / two unclean distinction is no proof of two fused accounts. Strongest single harmonization because it answers the named skeptic head-on. Single hyphens used as dashes in the source are kept verbatim (not the spec's allowed '--' case).
